clue.text: Theatrical release of captive with key, saying sorry

parts.note: Esc is the escape key on a computer keyboard
an apology is a way of saying sorry

explanation.surface: A captive is freed in some stage drama, with a key and an apology thrown in.
explanation.definitionFit: Escapology is the performing art of getting out of chains and locks, Houdini-style, as a stage act.

clue.text: Score, and the rest start to hug

parts.note: etc, et cetera, means and the rest

indicators.note: the start of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A tally of a match, with the rest beginning to embrace.
explanation.definitionFit: To score a surface is to scratch lines into it, as etching does.

clue.text: Rowers on canal identifying arrangement of locks

parts.note: a crew is a team of rowers
a cut is a man-made waterway, a canal

explanation.surface: Rowers on a canal work out how the locks are arranged.
explanation.walkthrough: 'locks' looks like canal locks but means hair.
explanation.definitionFit: A crew cut is a very short haircut, so a way of arranging locks of hair.

clue.text: Left the blaze raging around independent African city

parts.note: port is the left side of a ship

indicators.note: around means the scrambled letters surround the next piece
raging suggests the letters are in turmoil, rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone flees a fire raging around a free city in Africa.
explanation.walkthrough: 'raging' rearranges the anagram's letters into ELZABETH, which 'around' wraps round I. 'Left' is the ship's side, not departed.
explanation.definitionFit: Port Elizabeth is a South African coastal city in the Eastern Cape, now officially Gqeberha.

clue.text: Thin declining small shark?

indicators.note: declining is taken as refusing, so the item is turned away

parts.note: slender means thin

explanation.surface: A slim, small shark that is shrinking away.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that 'shark' is a loan shark, not a fish.
explanation.definitionFit: A loan shark is a moneylender, so a shark of that kind is one who lends.

clue.text: Gambler bringing up son that keeps track of consumption

indicators.note: in a down entry bringing up means a letter is lifted higher in the word

parts.note: a gamester is a gambler

explanation.surface: A gambler raises a son who keeps an eye on spending.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bringing up' lifts S earlier in GAMESTER.
explanation.definitionFit: A gas meter records how much fuel a household uses.

clue.text: Leap from plane with tail on fire

parts.note: a common word for an aeroplane driven by turbine engines

indicators.note: the tail of a word is its final letter, so only the end of fire is taken

explanation.surface: A parachutist leaps from an aircraft whose rear end is ablaze.
explanation.definitionFit: A jeté is a ballet jump from one foot to the other, so it is a leap.

clue.text: European guitar players missing piano star

indicators.note: missing means the letter is left out

parts.note: plectra, picks, are what play a guitar's strings
P is the musical abbreviation for piano, softly

explanation.surface: A European band's guitarists lack a pianist and their star.
explanation.walkthrough: 'players' suggests musicians but means picks.
explanation.definitionFit: Electra is one of the Pleiades, a star in that cluster.

clue.text: Show people around Stratford

definitions.meaning: ... are people from London's East End, where Stratford lies

explanation.surface: A display featuring people from the Stratford area.
explanation.walkthrough: Stratford here is the East London district, not Shakespeare's town.
explanation.definitionFit: The soap is a television programme, and residents of East London are known by that name.

clue.text: Companion stumbling over new road sign

parts.note: CH stands for Companion of Honour, a British order

indicators.note: stumbling suggests the letters of the word that follows totter into a new order

explanation.surface: A walking companion trips over a freshly laid road.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stumbling' scrambles OVER into EVRO.
explanation.definitionFit: Chevrons are the V-shaped arrows on road signs marking sharp bends.

clue.text: Masks, etc used by Republican in specialist regiment, and another

indicators.note: in says the next pieces sit inside the regiment's letters

parts.note: the SAS (Special Air Service) is a specialist British army regiment

indicators.note: used by places the equipment ahead of the party member who uses it

parts.note: PPE is personal protective equipment, such as masks and gloves

explanation.surface: Elite soldiers and a second unit are kitted out with masks and kit by an American politician.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition leans on the clue: 'another' means another specialist regiment besides the SAS.
explanation.definitionFit: Sappers are the Royal Engineers, a further specialist unit of the British Army, so another regiment.

clue.text: Reprising rap, he performs with finest artistic style

indicators.note: performs suggests the letters act out a new arrangement

parts.note: reprising the next word means doing it a second time, so it supplies another copy of it
the elite are the finest

explanation.surface: A rapper repeats a song, performing with the best musicians in an arty way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reprising' supplies a second RAP; 'performs' mixes RAP, RAP and HE into PRERAPHA.
explanation.definitionFit: Pre-Raphaelite names the Victorian movement of painters such as Rossetti and Millais.

clue.text: Emcee and minder ejecting one that's drunk the liqueur

indicators.note: drunk suggests the letters are reeling into a new arrangement
ejecting means throwing something out of what precedes it

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A compère and a bouncer throw out a drunk at a club, then share a liqueur.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ejecting' removes I from EMCEE MINDER; 'drunk' then mixes EMCEE MNDER into CREMEDEMEN.
explanation.definitionFit: Crème de menthe is a sweet green mint-flavoured liqueur.

clue.text: Icy roads may be such a devil when black

parts.note: an imp is a little devil
as can mean when, as in 'as I left'
sable is black in heraldry

explanation.surface: Icy roads can be a menace, especially with black ice.
explanation.definitionFit: Icy roads can be impossible to travel on, so they may be blocked.

clue.text: Master and kids discussed mathematical table

indicators.note: discussed means spoken out, so the pieces are heard rather than read

parts.note: MA is Master (of Arts), and to kid is to trick, giving MA TRICKS

explanation.surface: A schoolmaster and pupils talk over a times table in a maths lesson.
explanation.definitionFit: A matrix is a rectangular array of numbers in rows and columns, a table used in mathematics.

clue.text: On first part of journey maybe ring about help with cases?

parts.note: the opening stage of a journey could be called leg A, the first leg

indicators.note: about signals turning the word round, back to front

parts.note: to ring someone is to dial them

explanation.surface: Phoning someone at the start of a trip to ask for a hand with suitcases.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' turns DIAL into LAID. 'cases' looks like luggage but means court cases.
explanation.definitionFit: Legal aid is public funding that pays lawyers for people who cannot afford their court cases.

clue.text: Insurgent clothes touring American carried mainly, so to speak

indicators.note: touring means going round, so the word encloses the letter
insurgent means rising up, so in a down entry the word is read upwards

parts.note: to enrobe is to dress, so enrobes means clothes

explanation.surface: A rebel's garments travel round the States, carried for the most part.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Insurgent' turns ENROBES upwards into SEBORNE; 'touring' puts it round A. 'mainly' is the main, the sea, not 'mostly'.
explanation.definitionFit: The main is a poetic word for the sea, so goods carried by sea are carried on the main.

clue.text: A-Z map briefly reviewed before stay in Derby?

indicators.note: before puts the reversed piece ahead of the rest
reviewed is taken as re-viewed, looked at backwards
briefly means cut short, losing the final letter

parts.note: a plan is a map, as of a town

indicators.note: in says one word is placed inside the hat

parts.note: in America a derby is a bowler hat
to be is to stay or exist

explanation.surface: A London street atlas is checked before an overnight stay at the Derby races.
explanation.walkthrough: The A-Z is a well-known British street atlas, a decoy here; Derby is not the race but the American word for a bowler hat. 'briefly', 'reviewed' and 'in' work as the parse shows.
explanation.definitionFit: A to Z covers every letter, so it stands for the whole set of letters in order.

clue.text: Ancient city failing to fulfil Portsmouth couple

indicators.note: failing to fulfil means the word stops short of its finish

parts.note: Pompey is the nickname of Portsmouth, the English naval city and its football club
II is the Roman numeral for two, a couple

explanation.surface: An ancient city that a couple from Portsmouth fail to live up to.
explanation.definitionFit: Pompeii was the Roman town buried by Vesuvius in AD 79.

clue.text: Drink following each Xmas (beer) all reduced by half

indicators.note: every one of the three words is cut in half, keeping its second half

explanation.surface: Someone notes what they drink after every Christmas pint, now down to half measures.
explanation.definitionFit: A chaser is a drink taken straight after another, such as a whisky after a beer.

clue.text: Rogue meets some Greek for business lunch?

indicators.note: rogue suggests the letters behave unruly and break their order

parts.note: nu is a letter of the Greek alphabet, some Greek

explanation.surface: A rogue meets a Greek for a working lunch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rogue' rearranges MEETS as SETME. A set menu is often offered at business lunches.
explanation.definitionFit: A set menu is a fixed-price meal, the kind typically eaten at a working lunch.

clue.text: Perhaps Durham prison sounded dramatic

indicators.note: sounded means spoken out, so the spelling follows the pronunciation

parts.note: Durham is a see, a bishop's diocese, and nick is slang for prison: see nick

explanation.surface: Durham jail made a theatrical impression.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Perhaps' signals Durham is one example of a see.
explanation.definitionFit: Scenic can mean relating to stage scenery, theatrical.

clue.text: Writer's series of holy books current estate regularly discarded

parts.note: Samuel is a pair of Old Testament books, 1 and 2 Samuel
a beck is a stream, a current of water

indicators.note: every other letter is thrown away, leaving the alternate ones

explanation.surface: A writer's religious volumes go downstream while the estate is periodically thrown out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly discarded' drops S, A and E from ESTATE, leaving ETT. The 's is 'is', linking definition to wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Samuel Beckett was the Irish playwright and novelist who wrote Waiting for Godot.

clue.text: Talk up front in hall on variable exercises

indicators.note: the front of a word is its first letter

parts.note: Y is an algebraic variable
PE is physical education, exercises

explanation.surface: Someone at the front of a hall promotes a changing exercise routine.
explanation.definitionFit: To hype is to promote something extravagantly, boosting it in publicity.

clue.text: In Scotland, gas bill lacks content — it's different there

indicators.note: lacking its content means the inside of the word is emptied, leaving only its ends
different suggests the letters of the next word appear in another order

explanation.surface: A Scottish gas bill comes with no detail, and people say things are done differently there.
explanation.walkthrough: 'different' rearranges THERE as ETHER. 'gas' looks like fuel but means idle talk.
explanation.definitionFit: Blether is Scots for chatter or idle talk, and gas is slang for empty chat.

clue.text: One's in part of church and cathedral sharing echo, in innocence

indicators.note: in places the numeral inside the church part

parts.note: the nave is the main body of a church
I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: sharing means the letter is used once for both words, so the cathedral's copy is not written again

parts.note: Ely is a cathedral city in Cambridgeshire, a crossword favourite
Echo is E in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Someone stands in the nave as the cathedral's echo rings round them, in innocence.
explanation.walkthrough: NAIVE and ELY overlap on one shared E, so 'sharing echo' drops ELY's E.
explanation.definitionFit: To act naively is to act with innocence, so the adverb means in an innocent way.

clue.text: Visualised double measure of Chianti featuring in retreat

indicators.note: in retreat says the hidden letters are read backwards
a measure of the wine is just a part of it, so some letters are taken from inside these words

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A double measure of Chianti is pictured being drunk while on retreat.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft read 'measure' as part of the definition, but 'measure of' is the signal that the letters lie inside 'Chianti featuring'; the definition is 'Visualised double'.
explanation.definitionFit: An e-fit is an electronic composite of a suspect's face, a visual likeness or lookalike built from witness accounts.

clue.text: Arrange further scripture class to avoid returning after school

indicators.note: after places the turned-round word behind the school abbreviation

parts.note: RE is religious education, a school subject

indicators.note: returning means the word comes back the other way

parts.note: to elude is to avoid

explanation.surface: A school timetable change lets pupils skip a scripture class.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returning' turns ELUDE into EDULE.
explanation.definitionFit: To reschedule is to fix a new time, so to set up or plan again.
